name: Left Ventricle
description: Main pumping chamber of the heart. Thick-walled muscular chamber that ejects oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation via the aortic valve. On cardiac CTA: assess wall thickness, wall motion abnormalities, trabeculations, mural thrombus, and calculate LVEF. Apical thinning may indicate prior infarct.

name: Right Ventricle
description: Thin-walled anterior chamber that pumps deoxygenated blood to the pulmonary circulation via the pulmonary valve. Normally crescent-shaped in cross-section. On cardiac CTA: assess for dilatation (RV:LV ratio >1.0 suggests right heart strain), wall hypertrophy, and RVEF.

name: Left Atrium
description: Posterior superior chamber receiving oxygenated blood from the four pulmonary veins. On cardiac CTA: assess for dilatation (associated with atrial fibrillation), thrombus in the left atrial appendage (LAA), and pulmonary vein anatomy prior to ablation.

name: Right Atrium
description: Right-sided chamber receiving systemic venous return from the SVC and IVC. Contains the sinoatrial node (pacemaker), crista terminalis, and Eustachian valve. On cardiac CTA: assess for dilatation, thrombus, and central line position.

name: Ascending Aorta
description: Largest artery in the body. Ascending aorta arises from the aortic valve, arches over the left main bronchus, then descends through the thorax. On CT: assess diameter at standard levels (sinuses, mid-ascending, arch, isthmus, descending), wall calcification, intramural hematoma, dissection flap, and ulceration.

name: Pulmonary Trunk
description: Short wide vessel arising from the right ventricle, bifurcating into right and left pulmonary arteries at the level of the carina. On CT: main PA diameter >29 mm suggests pulmonary hypertension. Assess for pulmonary embolism (filling defects), aneurysm, and PA:aorta ratio.

name: Interventricular Septum
description: Muscular and membranous wall separating the left and right ventricles. The muscular portion is thick and contractile; the thin membranous portion is located superiorly near the aortic valve. On cardiac CTA: assess thickness (hypertrophy in HCM), septal defects (VSD), and wall motion.

name: Pericardium
description: Double-layered fibroserous sac surrounding the heart. The visceral layer (epicardium) adheres to the heart; the parietal layer is the outer fibrous sac. On cardiac CTA: assess for effusion, thickening (>4 mm suggests constrictive pericarditis), calcification, and pericardial masses.
